profile.name: Jesse Chen
profile.headline: Building technology that solves real problems for real people
profile.claim: Secure mobile, AI, and full-stack systems.
profile.description: Computer science student at Carnegie Mellon building secure mobile, AI, and full-stack systems that solve real problems.

experiences.summary: Architect and principal author of Bark, Carnegie Mellon’s campus AI assistant, leading 25 engineers. Bark grounds every answer in live university data.
Rebuilt billing and payment flows in an Android app with 500K+ members, and built a replay engine that found authentication flaws across 220+ API endpoints.
Rebuilt the main screens of a 10K+ user Flutter app, cut its homepage load time about 75%, and built shade matching on a color engine written from scratch.
Built the Python pipeline that turns OpenStreetMap and ArcGIS records into the building data behind CMUMaps, Carnegie Mellon’s campus map for 12K+ users.

experiences.summary: Built Unreal Engine 5 gameplay systems for grappling, tethering, and local multiplayer combat.

projects.name: ParkiWell
projects.lead: An app for managing everyday life with Parkinson’s, with symptom tracking, medication reminders, and guided speech and movement practice.
bullets: ParkiWell brings symptom logs, dose reminders, weekly practice plans, and peer support into one place. It helps people keep up with daily routines and look back at what’s changed.

The motion coach, currently in development, uses the phone’s camera to count reps and give live feedback for ten seated and standing exercises. Audio and vibration cues help people follow along, with extra time for slower movements.

Built with Flutter, a custom motion engine, and a Supabase backend. Health records are encrypted on the phone and stay available offline, with optional account backup. Camera footage stays on the device.

caseStudy.challenge: Symptoms, medication schedules, and regular practice can be difficult to keep track of. ParkiWell brings those routines together in an app designed to stay usable when tapping is difficult, movement is slower, or the connection drops.
approach: Designed symptom logs, dose reminders, weekly practice plans, and an optional community around everyday use, with large controls, screen-reader support, and protection against accidental repeat taps.

Built a motion coach that uses MediaPipe to follow 33 body points through the phone camera. A custom Dart engine counts reps and gives movement feedback through text, speech, and vibration, while keeping camera footage on the device.

Stored health records locally with AES-256 encryption so tracking works offline. Changes sync to Supabase when a connection returns, with database access rules that keep each account’s private records separate.
outcomes: Daily symptom and dose tracking that works offline
Motion coach in development with ten seated and standing exercises
Camera processing on the phone, with no video uploads

projects.name: Agoriai
projects.lead: A student career network for sharing interview experiences, comparing internships, and making connections under an alias.
bullets: Students can ask questions, browse company discussions, and message peers before deciding whether to share their name. Four visibility settings control the details attached to posts and comments, and name sharing in messages requires agreement from both people.
The Nexus uses D3 to map relationships between students and companies. Connections and company posts give each link its weight, helping people explore who has experience with a company.

Built in 36 hours at TartanHacks 2026 with React, a Bun/Elysia backend, and PostgreSQL. A custom moderation filter checks for abusive text, including attempts to disguise it with misspellings or hidden characters.

images.alt: Agoriai Nexus map showing connections between students and companies

images.label: agoriai.app / career activity
images.alt: Agoriai dashboard with career discussions and network activity

caseStudy.challenge: Students need ways to ask career questions and learn from peers before attaching their real name to a conversation. Agoriai brings those discussions together with company information and ways to discover relevant people.
approach: Applied four visibility settings to post and comment authors on the server. Direct messages use a separate request-and-accept flow before either person’s real name is revealed.
Used D3 to arrange students and companies in an interactive network, with links weighted by connections and company posts. Hovering highlights related people and companies.
Connected the React interface to 36 API endpoints through Bun and Elysia, with Drizzle managing PostgreSQL data. Moderation checks normalize disguised text, and session tokens are stored as hashes.
outcomes: Four visibility settings for posts and comments
Name sharing by mutual agreement in messages
Interactive discovery through student and company connections

projects.name: Tarocchi
projects.lead: A tarot game that turns a personal question into an illustrated adventure, with a reading shaped by the cards and choices along the way.
bullets: Players choose a spread, enter a question, and move through a shuffled selection of five illustrated settings. Each scene offers three choices that become part of the final reading.
A React reducer keeps track of the spread, scene order, and answers. An Express backend sends that context and the randomly drawn cards to Claude, which writes the reading in the guide’s voice.
CSS animations add drifting backgrounds, particles, and tilting cards, with optional background music. Built by a team of four in two days at HackCMU 2025.

caseStudy.challenge: The idea was to make a tarot reading feel like a short game, with room to explore before seeing the cards. The final interpretation needed to connect the player’s question and choices to the drawn spread.
approach: Used a React reducer to manage the spread, shuffled scene order, and player choices from the opening prompt through the result.
Combined Sarah Seekins’s 78-card PixelTarot deck with five illustrated settings, CSS parallax, particle effects, and optional looping music.
Passed the question, choices, and drawn cards through an Express backend to Claude. The cards are random, while the player’s answers give the interpretation its context.
outcomes: Three spreads with three, four, or five cards
Five illustrated settings with choices along the way
Claude readings grounded in the question, choices, and cards

projects.name: MyCommunity
projects.tag: Scout troops and service · Android prototype
projects.lead: An Android prototype designed to help families find Scout troops and give leaders a starting point for their next community service project.
bullets: Brings a troop map, service organizations, current news, and troop profiles into four sections. Guest browsing keeps the app open to families who are still exploring.
The Google Maps integration is designed to turn Firebase troop records into pins, with automatic framing and a different color for the leader’s own troop. Location access is optional.
Built in Java with Google Sign-In for the troop profile flow. The news feed loads New York Times stories through OkHttp and Gson, while Glide caches article images.
terminal: Android prototype for troops and service

caseStudy.challenge: Families need a starting point for finding a troop, and leaders need ideas for service projects. MyCommunity explores bringing a troop map, organization listings, and current news together in one Android app. It remains a prototype; live troop profiles still need Firebase authentication connected to the database access rules.
approach: Built mapping logic that turns Firebase troop records into named Google Maps pins, highlights the leader’s own troop, and adjusts the view to fit the available locations.
Added guest browsing, optional location permissions, and Google Sign-In for the troop profile form. Names, contact emails, and coordinates are checked before a profile is submitted.
Paired five service-organization listings with a New York Times news feed. OkHttp and Gson load the stories asynchronously, and Glide caches their images for smoother browsing.
outcomes: Four sections for troop discovery and service planning
News browsing with cached article images
